graphs.title: The pH falls as the hydrogen ion concentration rises.
graphs.label: pH

sentences: Compare a concentration of 0.001 mol/dm3 with 1 mol/dm3.
title: The pH scale and hydrogen ion concentration
goal: See how the pH of a solution changes with the concentration of hydrogen ions.
note: The pH of a solution is a measure of its hydrogen ion concentration: pH = -log10 of the concentration in mol/dm3. A higher concentration of hydrogen ions gives a lower pH.

predict.prompt: If the hydrogen ion concentration becomes ten times bigger, what happens to the pH?
predict.reveal: Set the concentration to 0.1 mol/dm3 and then to the smallest value and compare the pH.

concept_check.question: Which solution is more acidic?
options: The one with the lower pH
The one with the higher pH
concept_check.explanation: A lower pH means a higher hydrogen ion concentration, so the solution with the lower pH is more acidic.
